transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jon Park (Redwood CSM); Alicia Torres (Prism Head of ML), Derek Hsu (Prism Platform Eng), Nora Patel (Prism Finance), Samir Reddy (Prism SecOps)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Review of usage trends (sustained growth, spike pattern during batch jobs).
- Cost drivers: embedding-heavy endpoints + insufficient prefix caching.
- Tradeoff discussion: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for cost predictability and compliance.
- Next steps: benching, forecast, pricing options, pilot kickoff.

Topics: usage trends, cost optimization, reliability (p95/p99), rollout plan, compliance and KMS, Dedicated sizing, rightsize playbook.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: All right, hi everyone thanks for carving out time. this is Maya from Redwood, i'll kick it off, then Ravi will go into the bench and options. quick check - can everybody hear me?
[00:08] Alicia: yep loud and clear, thanks Maya.
[00:11] Derek: yep good here.
[00:15] Maya: great. quick agenda, 1) walk usage & cost trends, 2) surface reliability pain, 3) discuss options to rightsize (Dedicated/reserved, quantization, cache), 4) agree next steps. sound ok?
[00:26] Nora: sounds good, and i'll flag finance questions at the end.
[00:29] Maya: perfect. so Alicia over to you for a 2-3 minute update on where Prism is with rollout.
[00:34] Alicia: yeah sure, we've gone from beta to prod for our recommendations engine over the last quarter. roughly 3.8 million tokens/day average, but we see big spikes in the evening window when batch enrichment runs, that's pushing some p99 latency higher, and costs — embeddings have ballooned because we re-run top-N every hour.
[00:56] Maya: 3.8M tokens/day thats useful. do you have percentiles you can share quickly? p50/p95/p99?
[01:03] Alicia: p50 is ~80ms, p95 around 420ms, p99 at 1.8s for the text-gen endpoints. embeddings endpoints are slower of course, p95 ~1.2s p99 3.6s for larger batches.
[01:20] Ravi: quick clarifying q — are the p99s on hosted or are those against the dedicated pool you tested?
[01:26] Alicia: all on our current hosted account with Redwood, no dedicated yet, running at on-demand config.
[01:33] Ravi: got it, that helps. and when you say batch enrichment, that's synchronous requests during the window or async?
[01:39] Alicia: synchronous to keep pipeline simple, but we could move to async, yes.
[01:44] Maya: cool. ok costs — Nora, do you want to give the finance signal?
[01:49] Nora: yes. Costs grew 34% q/q with embeddings and longer contexts being the top line drivers. we're getting close to the threshold where a reserved commit or dedicated plan would start to make sense, but we need confidence on stable throughput and the right sizing. we can't offboard capacity mid-quarter without a clear playbook.
[02:08] Maya: totally understood. this is where our rightsize playbook comes in — it's a combination of forecast + bench + autoscale policy + quantization recommendation. Ravi can talk about the bench we recommend.
[02:19] Ravi: sure. so our immediate recommendation is a 2-hour bench that replays your sample traffic at 1.5x to measure tail latency under load, test prefix/KV cache hit rates, and compare two quantization profiles. we'll capture p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, and token/sec. sample artifacts: a perf spreadsheet, flamegraphs, and a small trace deck.
[02:36] Derek: quick q — for the bench, do you need us to export the entire traffic? we have privacy concerns for user PII.
[02:42] Ravi: we usually accept an anonymized CSV of request sizes, timestamps, and route IDs. if you want, we can run the bench in your VPC so none of the payload leaves your network.
[02:51] Samir: about that, we need to align on KMS/RSA/HSM — our security team won't permit keys outside our HSM for embeddings with pii. what's Redwood's stance?
[03:01] Maya: we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations on Private deployments; for Hosted we have envelope encryption and bring-your-own-keys with a limited trust boundary. Jon can follow up with the security pack.
[03:12] Jon Park: yes i'll share our security packet and the integration notes, also SOC2, ISO attestation links.
[03:17] Alicia: thanks, that's helpful. on the cost side what's a rough delta between staying hosted vs moving to Dedicated?
[03:24] Maya: ballpark: for steady-state high throughput a Dedicated pool with reserved commitment reduces per-token cost by 25-40% depending on utilization and batching. but there's an upfront commitment tradeoff and some capex feel. the math depends on headroom and burst patterns.
[03:38] Nora: can you share a scenario model? i.e., commit x for savings y, how would we structure it for our traffic shape?
[03:45] Maya: yes that's one of the deliverables — a tailored forecast model. we'll show break-evens across 3, 6, 12 month horizons and include burst credit policies.
[03:55] Ravi: another lever is intelligent batching + prefix/KV caching — if you can shift the enrichment job to hit the cache or run async the token churn drops a lot, that's low-hanging fruit before committing to Dedicated.
[04:07] Derek: for embeddings we do many small 16-32 vector requests; is there benefit from aggregate batching?
[04:11] Ravi: yes, if you can batch those into larger micro-batches, throughput improves and unit cost drops significantly. we can also recommend a quantization profile which trims model size at minimal quality loss for embeddings.
[04:21] Alicia: what about model variants for fallbacks — we have some regional latency issues and want graceful degradation during spikes.
[04:27] Maya: Redwood supports routing policies and compatible model variants. you can set rules to route by region, latency threshold, or cost tier; during a spike it falls back to a faster, cheaper variant. we also have automatic retry/backoff policies.
[04:40] Derek: ok, that sounds promising. one other ask — can you produce a cost visualization per-route/token-type? we need that for our exec.
[04:47] Jon Park: yes we have a per-route breakdown in console and can export a CSV. Maya will include a sample export in the deck.
[04:53] Nora: i'd like to see forecast plus sensitivity to 10/20/50% growth.
[04:58] Maya: noted.
[05:00] [Background chatter - brief cross talk]
[05:10] Ravi: quickly on reliability — your p99 of 1.8s on gen endpoints suggests tail queuing. two things to check: 1) KV cache hit rate (if low, warmups cost tokens), 2) batching/backpressure configuration. if you want we can instrument traces that show queue latencies.
[05:26] Derek: we actually saw cache hit rates around 12% during peak window, that's low.
[05:31] Ravi: yep that matches. increasing cache TTL for enrichment paths and pre-warming common prefixes should help.
[05:36] Alicia: there's also a concern about model regression detection — we had a subtle quality drop after a prompt tweak. how do you recommend we handle guardrails?
[05:45] Maya: our Optimize feature ties prompt sets and evals to rollouts, so you can block or auto-rollback on metric drift. we'll include a short walkthrough in the follow-up deck.
[05:55] Samir: security question — audit logs retention, can we keep 12 months of full request logs? and can they be routed to our SIEM?
[06:04] Jon Park: yes, longer retention is an add-on. logs can be forwarded to customer SIEM or stored in your VPC depending on Private plans.
[06:11] Samir: good.
[06:13] Maya: ok let's talk pilot options briefly — conservative route is a 3-month Dedicated pilot with autoscaling and a small reserved commit. aggressive route is Immediate Dedicated commit with larger upfront discount. alternatively a Private deployment (VPC) for your compliance-sensitive workloads.
[06:28] Nora: finance lean toward pilot first — minimize commitment, validate savings.
[06:32] Alicia: product wise we need guaranteed latency for live traffic, so can the pilot have SLOs?
[06:38] Maya: yes we can set SLO targets for the pilot and include rollback/fallback policies. the pilot contract will list p95/p99 targets and credits if missed.
[06:46] Derek: implementation-wise — how long to stand up a Dedicated pool?
[06:49] Ravi: typically 3-7 business days for initial pool provisioning and routing; Private/VPC takes longer depending on network approvals.
[06:57] Alicia: and data residency? we have EU customers, any constraints?
[07:00] Maya: we have regions in eu-west and can route EU traffic to EU-only pools, yes.
[07:05] Nora: ok great.

[07:10] -- (15 minute mark summary and mid-call recaps omitted for brevity) --

[22:15] Ravi: (bench design detail) when we replay traffic we'll use 1.5x burst to stress tail and isolate noisy neighbors, measure GPU saturation and token latencies, and try two quant profiles: q8_0 and q4_0 as candidates. we'll log KV hits and provide a sample runbook for capacity scaling.
[22:34] Derek: that q4 sounds aggressive, any quality tradeoff?
[22:38] Ravi: minimal for embeddings and some gen workloads; we'll validate with your eval set. if quality drop is >2% on your metric we won't recommend the profile.
[22:48] Alicia: how do we instrument to catch drift? is it per-prompt or per-route?
[22:52] Maya: both — Optimize supports route-level evals and can also run per-prompt checks at rollout.

[31:05] Nora: on the cost model, include both per-token and per-inference overheads, and show the effect of moving enrichment to async.
[31:13] Maya: will do.

[38:40] Samir: small question about IAM and RBAC — we need role separation between SRE and data-science teams; can our SAML map to Redwood roles?
[38:47] Jon Park: yes SAML/SSO with role mapping and granular RBAC is supported; we'll provide the STM mapping doc.

[45:02] Alicia: ok decision asks — we want bench asap, pricing scenarios, and an SLO-backed pilot plan. who's on point?
[45:10] Maya: on point: Maya for pricing & forecast, Ravi for bench, Jon for security docs, and Jon + Maya for pilot contract.
[45:19] Derek: i'll upload the sample traffic CSV and env variables to the shared folder after this call.
[45:25] Maya: perfect. one last question from finance — Nora?
[45:29] Nora: just want clarity on billing cadence during pilot and overage treatment.
[45:34] Maya: pilot will be billed monthly with overage split rules; we'll include exact terms in the deck.

[55:10] Final recap:
- Bench scheduled: Ravi runs bench and returns artifacts (traces, flamegraphs, spreadsheet).
- Pricing: Maya sends tailored forecast and pricing tiers.
- Security: Jon sends security packet and KMS integration notes.
- Customer to share traffic CSV and confirm compliance scope.

[55:40] Maya: ok thanks everyone great sync. we'll follow up with the deck and next-steps doc; expect everything in the next 48-72 hours.
[55:50] Alicia: thanks all, appreciate it.
[55:53] Derek: thanks.
[55:55] Nora: thanks bye.
[55:58] Maya: bye.
